findings.description: Critical: D1 and task 3.1 require JSON Schema, OpenAPI, Python, and TypeScript to accept the same context objects, but the structural schemas and generated TypeScript still admit objects that Python rejects. Draft-2020-12 validation accepts a traceparent whose embedded IDs differ from trace_id/span_id (and an attempt_number unrelated to claim_generation), while the Pydantic model rejects it; the TypeScript aliases are plain string and an entirely invalid OperationContextEnvelope compiles without invoking any guard.
findings.resolution: Freeze one composite semantic validation contract and generate an equivalent parser/validator for every runtime surface, including TypeScript tracestate, carrier equality, zero-ID, field-length, and generation-plus-one checks. If JSON Schema/OpenAPI remain structural-only because standard JSON Schema cannot express cross-field equality, change D1/task 3.1 to state that limitation and require all consumers to call the generated composite validator before accepting an envelope; add the reproduced mismatch object as a drift test.

findings.description: Critical: the SQL null-bypass is not fully closed. A non-null submission_context can contain JSON null for traceparent, trace_id, and span_id while the duplicated columns are SQL NULL; key-presence and size checks pass, every nullable column check passes, and IS NOT DISTINCT FROM considers each null pair equal. This contradicts the non-null envelope schema and the iteration-4 claim that every duplicate is required when canonical context exists.
findings.resolution: When submission_context is non-null, explicitly require submission_traceparent, trace_id, and submission_span_id to be non-null and require their JSON members to have string types/non-null values before equality/casts. Apply the same type/non-null validation to every required envelope member that SQL treats as canonical, retain legacy compatibility only for submission_context IS NULL, and add direct-SQL cases using JSON null for each duplicated field.

findings.description: Nit: the TypeScript signed-BIGINT guard tests an unbounded decimal regex and then constructs BigInt(value) before checking the 19-character contract limit, so a long digit string reaches an unnecessarily expensive arbitrary-precision parse even though every canonical value is at most 19 characters.
findings.resolution: Short-circuit on value.length <= 19 before the regex and BigInt conversion, and include an oversized digit-string case in the generated TypeScript guard tests.

findings.description: The revision correctly adds executable process-health lifecycle columns and exact expiry constraints, explicit claim-generation headroom, null-safe duplicate comparisons, bounded Python scalars, non-zero W3C identifiers, and a still-valid package DAG.
findings.resolution: Retain these fixes while closing the remaining semantic-validator and JSON-null gaps.
